subject: Clarify allocation for mixed-degradation incident (Aug 1819)
messages:
From: Pete Taylor <ptaylor@skyrisecloud.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: SkyRise Cloud Support <support@skyrisecloud.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Requesting SLO credit: Aug 18 partial throughput drop

Hi Aditya,

Our monitoring picked up a sustained throughput degradation on our API routes that hit Redwood between 2026-08-18 22:05 UTC and 2026-08-19 02:20 UTC. We saw a ~35-45% drop in request completion for a subset of prefixes (eu-west and us-east origin paths) rather than total outage. This materially affected background processing for us and triggered downstream job retries.

We opened support ticket #9832 (attached) but would like a formal SLA allocation and credit calculation per our contract (section 4.2). From our side:
- Impact window: 2026-08-18T22:05:00Z -> 2026-08-19T02:20:00Z
- Estimated affected traffic: ~18% of our Redwood token spend for that 4+ hour window
- We observed CDN vendor (thirdparty-edge) maintenance noted in their status at 2026-08-18T23:30Z -> 2026-08-19T00:45Z — wondering how that factors into Redwood's uptime accounting.

Attached: sla-report-2026-08-18-19.csv and our probe logs. Can you confirm how credits will be calculated for partial degradations that are not 100% downtime and where a third-party maintenance overlaps?

Thanks,
Pete Taylor
Head of Platform Operations
SkyRise Cloud

(Attachment: sla-report-2026-08-18-19.csv, edge-probe-logs-aug18-19.txt, support-ticket-#9832.pdf)

Pete,

Thanks for the note and the attachments — we received ticket #9832 and started an internal data pull. I'm looping in Marissa (CS lead) and Marcus (SRE) to validate the timeline and propose a credit calculation. A few quick clarifying questions so we can avoid back-and-forth: 
1) Can you confirm whether the 18% affected traffic estimate is measured by token spend or request count?
2) Are any customer-facing endpoints fully returning 5xx for you during the window, or was it uniformly higher latency / partial drops?

Next steps from our side: Marcus will run per-prefix availability and throughput deltas, and we'll map overlap with the third-party maintenance window you called out. We'll aim to send a proposed allocation and credit amount by next Tuesday (Aug 25).

Apologies for the impact — we'll prioritize this.

Best,

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 07:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Re: Requesting SLO credit: Aug 18 partial throughput drop

Aditya / Marissa,

I pulled the edge collector logs and ran a differential analysis across our health probes and customer telemetry. High level findings:
- Confirmed degraded throughput between 2026-08-18T22:03:00Z and 2026-08-19T02:24:00Z for the affected prefixes.
- Severity: system-level request completion dropped ~40% for requests routed via thirdparty-edge in eu-west & us-east (not all prefixes, ~22% of routes).
- Root cause: mix of thirdparty-edge congestion plus transient queuing on Reed-23 nodes (autoscaler transient lag under burst).
- Overlap: thirdparty-edge maintenance window (their published start 2026-08-18T23:30Z -> 2026-08-19T00:45Z) sits squarely inside the larger degraded window. Outside that window the Reed-23 queuing explains most of the remaining delta.

Policy implications: our SLA defines "unavailability" as inability to serve a request (5xx/timeout). Historically we've treated partial throughput degradations as eligible for proportional credit only when they cause a measurable increase in user-facing failed requests or exceed a configured latency SLO threshold. For this case: customer-supplied probes show higher retry rates, and internal failure rate increased from baseline 0.3% -> 3.1% during the window (so it crosses the failure-rate trigger).

Recommendation (two options):
A) Apportion entire credit proportional to affected spend for the full degradation window (4h21m) but discount the credit for the third-party maintenance interval since the customer contract excludes third-party planned maintenances if duly notified. That yields an effective credit of ~6.2% of monthly usage (quick calc attached).
B) Offer a compromise: 50% of the apportionment for the third-party overlap and full apportionment for the rest, producing ~7.6% credit. This recognizes some shared responsibility because Reed-23 autoscaler response was a driver.

Attached: edge-probe-logs-aug18-19.txt (raw), sla-calcs-20260821.csv (internal).

I'll let Marissa handle the commercial communication.

- Marcus
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Pete,

Thanks for your patience while we investigated. We've validated the timeline and ran the apportionment models Marcus recommended. Summary of our proposal:
- Affected window (validated): 2026-08-18T22:03:00Z -> 2026-08-19T02:24:00Z (4h21m)
- Measured customer-facing failure-rate delta: baseline 0.3% -> 3.1% during window
- Proposed credit: 7.0% of monthly Redwood spend applied to the billing period that included Aug 18-19.

Rationale: we applied option B (split the third-party maintenance overlap) to reflect shared responsibility — Redwood acknowledges the autoscaler queuing on Reed-23 nodes while also recognizing third-party-edge maintenance during the sub-window. We're attaching the detailed calc (sla-calcs-20260821.csv) and a short write-up in the Drive link: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/SkyRise-incident-2026-08.

If you accept, we'll issue a formal credit memo and apply it to your next invoice. If you'd like a different split, we're open to adjusting — please let us know which sections of the calc you'd like us to re-run.

Best,
Marissa Cole
